pr_title: drivers: flash: ospi for stm32 mcu
pr_body:
Fixes command configuration to have samples/drivers/spi_flash
passed on stm32l562 and stm32u585 disco kits.
The code is inspired from the [stm32Cube](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeL5/tree/master/Drivers/BSP) 


Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/46740

Signed-off-by: Francois Ramu <francois.ramu@st.com>
pr_comments:
samples/drivers/spi_flash tested on the  stm32l562 and stm32u585 disco kits in OPI/DTR modes

```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.1.0-586-gdf7f3121ab7d  ***

JEDEC OSPI-NOR SPI flash testing
==========================

Test 1: Flash erase
Flash erase succeeded!

Test 2: Flash write
Attempting to write 4 bytes                                                                      
Data read matches data written. Good!! 
```

successfully tested on stm32u5  disco kit : b_u585i_iot02 and stm32l562e_dk
OSPI flash config is OPI / DTR 
OSPI flash config is OPI / STR
OSPI configuring SPI|DUAL|QUAD / STR

On the disco kits stm32u5 and stm32l5, the octoflash does not answer to the read-sfdp. That's why a "dummy" 
sfdp-bfp table is inserted in the DTS. There is something wrong in getting the data->read_opcode and data->write_opcode. As a workaround, the read command.Instruction and write command.Instruction are set to their SPI_NOR_xxx CMD values (from the drivers/flash/spi_nor.h)

Unfortunately, I don't have any board with OSPI flash IC. Can test only against quad/dual ICs over OSPI (_i.e. MX25L12835F_).
However, current modifications will break OSPI for quad and dual modes, especially for some Winbond ICs (_lack of support for the hardcoded opcodes_). 

I suggest using the SFDP read opcodes and dummy cycles but allow DTS overrides. That way we shall cover most scenarios. At least for flash in SPI, Dual, and Quad modes (_OSPI mode can use hardcoded opcodes for now_).

Later on "JEDEC 4-byte Address Instruction" support could be implemented to get OSPI mode opcodes (_it seems that most OSPI flash ICs support it)_.

Address length can be detected by SFDP (_JESD216 1st DWORD_) and DTS can be used for overrides (_has to be checked for OSPI flash_).
set the  `s_command.InstructionMode = HAL_OSPI_INSTRUCTION_1_LINE` for all non-ospi modes
adding the `four-byte-opcodes;` property : must be set to have octoflash working in SPI mode

Rebase on 5897de1e535816247e309348cbe29760361a28b8
Set the 32/24 bits addressSize with  `cmd_pp.AddressSize = stm32_ospi_hal_address_size(dev);`  for the flash_stm32_ospi_write

Successfully tested on stm32u5 disco kit : b_u585i_iot02 and stm32l562e_dk
OSPI flash config is OPI / DTR
OSPI flash config is OPI / STR
OSPI configuring SPI|DUAL|QUAD / STR
```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.1.0-3175-g923410906b43  ***               
                                                                    
ospi-nor-flash@0 SPI flash testing                                              
==========================                                                      
                                                                                
Test 1: Flash erase                                                             
Flash erase succeeded!                                                          
                                                                                
Test 2: Flash write                                                             
Attempting to write 4 bytes                                                     
Data read matches data written. Good!!
```

issue_context.title: stm32 flash ospi fails on stm32l5 and stm32u5 disco
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When testing the samples/drivers/spi_flash on b_u585i_iot02a or stm32l562e_dk
the error occurs : "SPI flash driver MX25LM51245 was not found!"


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. west build -p auto -b stm32l562e_dk samples/drivers/spi_flash
2. west flash
3. See error

**Expected behavior**
```
JEDEC OSPI-NOR SPI flash testing
==========================

Test 1: Flash erase
Flash erase succeeded!

Test 2: Flash write
Attempting to write 4 bytes
Data read matches data written. Good!!
```


**Impact**
regression after the merge of the https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/45917



**Logs and console output**
```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.1.0-582-gcefd74f0444f  ***

JEDEC OSPI-NOR SPI flash testing                                            
==========================                                                  
SPI flash driver MX25LM51245 was not found!                                 
[00:00:05.141,000] <err> flash_stm32_ospi: OSPI AutoPoll failed             
[00:00:05.141,000] <err> flash_stm32_ospi: OSPI flash busy failed           
[00:00:05.141,000] <err> flash_stm32_ospi: OSPI mode not config'd (8 rate 2)
[00:00:05.141,000] <dbg> flash_stm32: stm32_flash_init: Flash initialized. BS: 8
[00:00:05.141,000] <dbg> flash_stm32: stm32_flash_init: Block 0: bs: 2048 count: 256
[00:00:05.141,000] <dbg> flash_stm32: stm32_flash_init: Block 1: bs: 0 count: 0
[00:00:05.141,000] <dbg> flash_stm32: stm32_flash_init: Block 2: bs: 0 count: 0
[00:00:05.141,000] <dbg> flash_stm32: flash_stm32_write_protection: Disable write protection
```



**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: ubuntu
 - Toolchain zephyr-sdk-0.14.0
 - Commit SHA : cefd74f0444fae745b12764890989dd3f01f0735

**Additional context**
comments:
In the stm32_ospi_write_enable() function, two commands are issued to the octoflash 
1.  with SPI_NOR_(O)CMD_WREN instruction
2.  with SPI_NOR_(O)CMD_RDSR instruction
In between some s_command parameters should be updated : .AddressMode, .DataMode

Also, I suspect a pb with the command.AddressSize and the stm32_ospi_hal_address_size badly init'd 
--> in the flash_stm32_ospi_write() 
  `cmd_pp.AddressSize = HAL_OSPI_ADDRESS_32_BITS;`

Refering to the [AN5050](https://www.st.com/content/ccc/resource/technical/document/application_note/group0/91/dd/af/52/e1/d3/48/8e/DM00407776/files/DM00407776.pdf/jcr:content/translations/en.DM00407776.pdf), the command.AddressSize is HAL_OSPI_ADDRESS_32_BITS except in quad mode.

review_comments:
Many dual and quad mode ICs use 1 line mode for that. 
By removing 

> `s_command.DataMode = HAL_OSPI_DATA_1_LINE;`

the mode is enforced to be 2 or 4 lines in the prepare cmd while it shall be 1 line.

Forcing the `s_command.DataMode = HAL_OSPI_DATA_1_LINE` for all non-ospi modes
after the prepare command which sets the  s_command.DataMode

Do you mean ` s_command.InstructionMode = HAL_OSPI_INSTRUCTION_1_LINE` too ?

> Do you mean s_command.InstructionMode = HAL_OSPI_INSTRUCTION_1_LINE too ?

Sorry, yes.
`ospi_prepare_cmd` already sets `s_command.AddressMode = HAL_OSPI_ADDRESS_8_LINES` and `s_command.DataMode = HAL_OSPI_DATA_8_LINES`  for `OSPI_OPI_MODE`.

yes for the WREN command but here is the RDSR command to be prepared, 
Just before (line 375)
```
	s_command.AddressMode = HAL_OSPI_ADDRESS_NONE;
	s_command.DataMode    = HAL_OSPI_DATA_NONE;
```
So for this new RDSR command AddressMode and DataMode may change

Many dual and quad mode ICs use 1 line mode for that.
By removing

> `s_command.InstructionMode = HAL_OSPI_INSTRUCTION_1_LINE;`

the mode is enforced to be 2 or 4 lines in the prepare cmd while it shall be 1 line.

forcing the `s_command.InstructionMode = HAL_OSPI_INSTRUCTION_1_LINE` for all non-ospi modes
after the prepare command which sets the s_command.DataMode

Quad and dual flashes might not work with a 32-bits address size.
`ospi_prepare_cmd` enforces 32-bits address size. Please use 24-bits for non `OSPI_OPI_MODE`.
forcing the s_command.InstructionMode = HAL_OSPI_INSTRUCTION_1_LINE for all non-ospi modes
